thread.title: Cowgirls advance to fifth place at Mountain West Women's Golf Championships

author: h. n. meeks
title: Cowgirls advance to fifth place at Mountain West Women's Golf Championships
text:
The Cowgirls women’s golf team moved up to fifth place in the team standings through 36 holes at the Mountain West Women’s Golf Championships at Mission Hills Country Club, according to an April 22 update.
The team’s advancement puts them ahead of Colorado State after a strong second round, signaling improved performance as the tournament progresses. The Cowgirls finished with a score of 293 (+5) during Wednesday’s second round on the par-72, 6,286-yard Dinah Shore Tournament Course and are now +16 for the tournament.
Kiley Reisner led Wyoming with a second-round score of 71 (-1), placing her tied for fourth in the individual competition. Reisner is one of only five players under par and trails leaders from Boise State, Grand Canyon, and Colorado State. Head coach Josey Stender said, “The team played with tremendous patience today. Especially down the stretch when the windy conditions made it difficult.”
Team members Elle Higgins and Meghan Vogt are tied for 21st place at +5 despite playing through injuries. Vogt and sophomore Kira Reisner each shot a 73 on Wednesday; Kira is tied for 27th overall at +7. Stender said, “I’m so grateful for the leadership Meg, Elle and Kira are showing with their mental toughness and confidence on this stage. Kiley continues to compete like a veteran and plays with tenacity. I’m excited for tomorrow’s finish.”
Grand Canyon currently leads in team scoring by one stroke over Nevada (+9), followed by UNLV (+10) and San Jose State (+13). Wyoming sits three shots behind San Jose State heading into Thursday’s final round.
With one round remaining in Rancho Mirage, fans can follow live results as teams compete for championship placement.
